audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer's win array gives Kayle Levels 2 and 3, while the prose on the same page says 'Kayle is one of the easiest early lanes you get', whys[1] 'she still has no ranged form or escape, so you keep shoving', and whys[2] 'even at level 3 she can't trade back in melee'. The packet's levelChart for this matchup reads Malphite for the first four stages and agrees with the prose — the stored win array is the outlier.
audit.why: Kayle is melee with no escape and no ranged form until Divine Ascent's range upgrade, which is the entire reason Malphite wins 54.83% over 797 games. Awarding her Levels 2-3 inverts the one thing every Kayle lane is about.
audit.corrected: Levels 2 and 3 should read Malphite; First item and 2+ items correctly stay Kayle. Blocked from proposing the flip — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait her R' is the page's central instruction, repeated in six places, and the cooldown is never given. Without the number the advice sounds like a minor tempo tip.
audit.why: Divine Judgment is 160/120/80s. A rank-1 Kayle who burns it has no answer for nearly three minutes — that is not a tempo tip, it is the whole lane. Set against Unstoppable Force at 130/115/100s, you get your ult back before she gets hers back at every rank, which is the actual mechanical reason the bait-then-commit plan works.
audit.corrected: The 160s number added so baiting her ultimate reads as the lane-deciding play it is.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup's most important interaction is absent from both layers: the page's entire plan is 'stack armour and out-trade her', and Kayle's Q undoes exactly that. Neither layer mentions it.
audit.why: Radiant Blast reduces the resistances of everyone it hits. Against Malphite that is a double hit — armour is his survivability AND his damage, since Ground Slam deals magic damage based on his armour. So every Radiant Blast that lands lowers your damage as well as your durability, which is why she can out-trade an armour stack the page assumes is safe. Two more missing pieces: Starfire Spellblade is an auto-attack reset dealing bonus damage proportionate to MISSING health, so it gets stronger exactly as the trade goes badly — the reset wind-up is the tell to disengage, not to keep trading. And Celestial Blessing (15s) heals her, which is what makes Grievous Wounds matter in the extended trade.
audit.corrected: Radiant Blast's resistance reduction stated as the counter to your own build, Starfire Spellblade's missing-health reset named as the burst tell, Celestial Blessing named as the heal to cut.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kayle.json (Q reduces resistances; E bonus damage on missing health; W heal)
champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (E: magic damage based on his Armor)

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Divine Judgment 160/120/80s is the one that decides commits. Radiant Blast is 12/11/10/9/8s and is her only ranged tool before her range upgrade, so a missed Q pre-6 is a free walk-up. Starfire Spellblade at 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s is the burst piece.
audit.corrected: Ult and Q numbers added as the two clocks worth tracking.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization carries the '(by his AD profile)' template leftover, and prescribes anti-heal as 'Thornmail component early' without naming what heals.
audit.why: Kayle is hybrid — physical autos plus magic on-hit and Divine Ascent's fire waves — so the TL;DR's 'build a little of both' is right and the item line should reflect mixed resists rather than pure armour. Celestial Blessing is the heal that anti-heal answers. Worth stating too that Radiant Blast's resistance reduction means raw stacking returns less here than the page implies.
audit.corrected: Mixed resists with Mercury's Treads kept, Celestial Blessing named as the heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags that neither layer names any Kayle ability — confirmed, both say only 'her R', 'her last-stack auto poke', 'ranged form'. The two suspect names it raised ('Ground Slam's', 'Seismic Shard's') are false positives.
audit.why: Real names are Divine Ascent, Radiant Blast, Celestial Blessing, Starfire Spellblade and Divine Judgment. Divine Ascent is the one that matters most and is never named: it is the passive that grants the attack range the whole late-game section depends on.
audit.corrected: Real names used; Divine Ascent named as the source of her ranged form.

edits.before: Kayle is one of the easiest early lanes you get — she is melee until level 6 with no escape, so I shove the wave, walk up, and Seismic Shard her every time she reaches for a last hit, stealing her move speed so she can't even back off cleanly. Granite Shield eats her weak auto poke and refreshes the second I disengage, so I take every trade. The whole plan pre-6 is to deny her farm and set up a dive; she has nothing to punish me with, so I play aggressive, not safe.
edits.after: Kayle is one of the easiest early lanes you get — melee until Divine Ascent grants her range, with no escape, so I shove the wave, walk up, and Seismic Shard her every time she reaches for a last hit, stealing her move speed so she can't back off cleanly. Granite Shield eats her weak auto poke and refreshes the second I disengage, so I take every trade. Her only outs are Celestial Blessing's heal and walking away. Deny farm, set up a dive, play aggressive.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still mine — Thunderclap stacks armor and adds AoE on-hit splash to my autos, and Ground Slam's attack-speed slow blunts her last-stack auto-attack poke, so I out-trade her flat and keep her off the wave. At 6 I get Unstoppable Force for a hard all-in, but here's the catch: her R grants full invulnerability, so if I commit R into an untouched Kayle she just presses it, I knock up nothing, and she walks. Bait her R or her summoners first, then engage. This is my last clean kill window before she scales.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still mine — Thunderclap stacks armor and adds AoE splash to my autos, and Ground Slam's attack-speed slow blunts her auto poke, so I out-trade her flat. Two cautions: Radiant Blast strips resistances, so it cuts my armor AND the Ground Slam damage that scales off it, and Starfire Spellblade is a reset that hits harder the lower I am. At 6 her Divine Judgment is full invulnerability — bait it and she is naked for 160s. That is my last clean kill window.

edits.before: This is where it flips, and I'm honest about it: once Kayle has 2+ items and her ranged form, she kites my short-range kit from outside Seismic Shard range and her Nashor's/Lich Bane on-hit DPS chews through my armor stacking faster than I can answer. Her R invulnerability simply turns off my Unstoppable Force on demand. I do not try to 1v1 a fed Kayle in a sidelane — I close the game on my early lead before she gets here, and if it goes long I use R to flank and knock up her whole team in a fight where she can't invuln out of everyone at once.
edits.after: This is where it flips, and I'm honest about it: with 2+ items and Divine Ascent's range she kites my short-range kit from outside Seismic Shard, and Radiant Blast strips the resistances my whole build rests on while her on-hit DPS chews through what's left. Divine Judgment turns off my engage on demand, and Celestial Blessing heals back the chip — bring Grievous Wounds. I don't 1v1 a fed Kayle in a sidelane; I close on my early lead, and if it runs long I flank with R and knock up her whole team, which she can't invuln out of at once.

notes: The decisive interaction was missing from both layers: Radiant Blast reduces the resistances of everyone it hits, and against Malphite that is a double hit because Ground Slam deals magic damage BASED ON HIS ARMOUR — so her Q lowers his damage and his durability with one cast, which is exactly the plan ('stack armour and out-trade her') the page recommends. LEVEL-CHART CONTRADICTION (unresolved): content win[] awards Kayle Levels 2 and 3 while the prose beside it says she is one of the weakest early champions in the game and cannot trade back in melee, and the packet levelChart agrees with the prose, not the array. Levels 2-3 should read Malphite; the flip exceeds the applier's 10% length band. That is the sixth matchup in this slice blocked by the band being applied to enum side/win fields — worth a targeted applier change rather than six hand fixes. Divine Judgment's 160s rank-1 cooldown is the single most useful number added here: the page said 'bait her R' six times without ever saying what baiting it buys you.
